title: To all of us who are enabled by AI
author: Careless_Road8873
selftext:
I'm from the 80s and I've been gaming for more than 30 years, from the 90s until now.

Of course I'd make a game overnight if I could.

Do it, play with it, show it to the close friends who have been gaming with you along the way.

If your aim is to market your game, market it to yourself and your close circle first.

Focus on making it as good as possible: art, mechanics, dynamics, sound, every part you've been exposed to all those years. You might lack the coding and art skills, or a game studio with the management and capital, but if you have that insight, the game will be played.

If you only focus on making a game and marketing it, you'll end up as noise.

comments.author: lophtt
comments.body:
My wife makes music and I think about that while I’m making my game; it’s a passion-project, for me, and if other people find it enjoyable, then great!

The AI part is like being given Bandcamp or something when you don’t know how to play an instrument very well; now you can bring your vision to life a bit easier but to do anything meaningful you still have to have interesting and creative ideas 🤷

comments.author: Fizassist1
comments.body:
dumb take.  as somebody who has tried many times over the years to teach myself, my best tutor to date has been chatgpt.  helped me set up the engine and walked me through setting up nodes and scripts to handle the behavior I wanted.

a lot of people dont have the time or resources to learn without AI assistance.  should those people be denied the right to be creative and make their vision a reality?  not with todays tools.

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: Not having a five-figure sum to hire contributors and that thing called *time* might be a factor. Let's not pretend we're all healthy unemployed childless singles.

comments.author: Fizassist1
comments.body: I did, and I learned a lot with AI too.  I just learned more and faster with gpt teaching me.  I know its hard for you to understand because "Ai BaD" or something..

comments.author: protheus99
comments.body: I tend to agree with this opinion but know that even a perfect game or app can't make it through the noise without lots of luck, I do wish you all the best and hope you got some marketing strategy to build a strong community also !

replies.author: Careless_Road8873
replies.body: Thank you. Passion on action creates inevitability =)

comments.author: Weasel_Redux
comments.body:
You don't know how timely this pep talk is! Once you start checking your itch.io stats hourly, you can lose sight of why you started developing in the first place.

I love my little game, and it's helped me develop skills in both using AI and managing projects. Sure, it would be ace if strangers picked it up and got as obsessed as I am, but the original goal of building something I can play with mates has been achieved.

Has your dev uncovered skills you didn't realise you had?

replies.author: Careless_Road8873
replies.body: Same here with the itch stats, I check them more than I'd like to admit. The skill that surprised me was art direction. I can't draw, but picking and throwing out hundreds of pictures taught me what I actually like.

replies.author: Weasel_Redux
replies.body:
I've been following one of the big AI art/slop threads on a dev sub and watching the vitriol against AI-generated artwork with interest. Art is such a huge part of a game, and if you're on your own, I think developing your own sense of style and keeping it consistent is not to be underestimated! I've started noticing faint shifts in my sepia tones, and I definitely have a few badge graphics that need regenerating.

Loving that I can now call it "art direction". That's going on the CV! 

Have you got a style guide or palette rules to keep you on the straight and narrow?

comments.author: Alone-Biscotti6145
comments.body:
I built a fan remake of the original COD Zombies map, shared it with my circle and family as a fun remake. It's free to play, I just built it for fun. To my surprise, it's actually doing pretty well on itch.

comments.author: Vaxi122654
comments.body: I wanted to have this conversation, what is it that makes people spend at most a month of time on their idea and submit it to Steam? Trust me, it looks bad. There's a reason real indie developers take 2-4 years to get something out the door. What's the rush?
